4 The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has notified the Environment Protection (Endof-Life Vehicles) Rules, 2025 ("the Rules') on January 6,
2025, which came into effect ftom April l, 2025. In accordance with the Rules, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) obligations are imposed on producers

4 The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has notified the Environment Protection (End-of-Life Vehicles) Rules, 2025 ("the
Rules") on January 6,2025, which came into effect from April 1,2025. ln accordance with the Rules, Extended Producer Responsibility
(EPR) obligations are imposed on producers ("vehicle manufacturers/lmporters") for the scrapping of End-of-Life Vehicles. As per the
Rules, such obligations are to be fulfilled through the purchase of EPR certificates from Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities via
Centralised Online Portal, which has been made partially operational. However, the pricing mechanism for EPR certificates, and
measurement framework for determining financial obligations are not yet made available.
Consequently, the Company is cunently unable to reliably estimate a range of possible outcomes and the impact will be evaluated once the
implementation framework for determining the reliable estimate is established.
